content: Sulfamethoxazole, marketed as Bactrim, is contraindicated for use in pediatric patients who are less than 2 months old. For the treatment of urinary tract infections (UTIs) and shigellosis in adults, the standard dosage is one Bactrim DS (double strength) tablet or two regular Bactrim tablets administered every 12 hours for a duration of 10 to 14 days. For shigellosis, the same daily dosage is used but for a shorter duration of 5 days. In pediatric patients with UTIs or acute otitis media, the recommended dosage is 40 mg/kg of sulfamethoxazole and 8 mg/kg of trimethoprim per 24 hours. This dosage is divided into two equal doses, administered every 12 hours for 10 days. For shigellosis in children, the same daily dosage is used for 5 days. For adults with acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis, the usual dosage is one Bactrim DS tablet or two regular Bactrim tablets every 12 hours for 14 days. For children requiring a lower limit dose, the guideline suggests administering 75% of the standard dose, which corresponds to 75 mg/kg of sulfamethoxazole and 15 mg/kg of trimethoprim per 24 hours. For pediatric patients, an alternative dosing regimen involves administering 750 mg/m²/day of sulfamethoxazole and 150 mg/m²/day of trimethoprim. This is given orally in two equally divided doses per day on three consecutive days each week. For the treatment of traveler’s diarrhea in adults, the standard dosage is one Bactrim DS tablet or two regular Bactrim tablets every 12 hours for 5 days.
